newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hundreds evacuated as floods cut off outback town.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hundreds evacuated as floods cut off outback town.

text.p: Hundreds of Australians have been evacuated from their homes after floodwaters cut off an outback town in Queensland state following four days of heavy rain, emergency authorities said on Tuesday.
The 3,500 strong town of Charleville, about 700km (430 miles) west of Brisbane, has been isolated since the Warrego River flooded on Monday, cutting rail and road links.
The Queensland goverment declared the town and surrounding region a natural disaster area, while flood warnings were issued for other river systems in the region.
"Most of south-west Queensland has got some level of flooding. It covers an extremely large area," a Queensland State Counter Disaster Centre spokesman said.
Hospital and nursing home patients in Charleville have been moved to other towns in the region, while helicopters have dropped food to outlying farms and helped with evacuations.
The Australian defence force was on Tuesday flying bedding, generators and field kitchens to the town, where about 400 people have been housed at a high school and sports ground.
More people were being evacuated on Tuesday.
In 1990, 1,000 homes in the town were flooded. Since then Charleville has suffered years of drought.
